# Spine: CLI-first application guide

> Create projects with Spine CLI, keep assembly in `BuildApplication`, and verify the execution contract and real behavior.

## Version and sources

This guide targets Spine `v0.7.1`. CLI `v0.4.3-rc.1` or later supports the current controller and dependency-channel features. Install a published stable CLI with `go install github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli/cmd/spine@latest`; check `spine version` before using these commands. Until a compatible stable CLI is published, the explicit candidate is `go install github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli/cmd/spine@v0.4.3-rc.1`. CLI version and application dependency channel are independent.

Core and CLI require Go 1.25.5 or later; playground validator and NATS require Go 1.26 or later. Core `v0.7.1` is published. The documented examples were tested with Echo `v0.2.0-rc.1`, net/http `v0.1.0-rc.1`, and playground `v0.2.0-rc.1`. Select published compatible stable platform tags when available. Preserve application source, `go.mod`, and `go.sum`; do not infer current publication state from an intended release.

- Documentation: /en/docs
- Installation: /en/learn/getting-started/installation
- First app: /en/learn/getting-started/first-app
- Platform choices: /en/learn/getting-started/platforms
- v0.7.1 migration: /en/learn/migration/v0.7.1
- HTTP inputs: /en/learn/migration/v0.7.1-preview
- Runtime OpenAPI: /en/reference/api/openapi
- Actual published tags: /en/community/versions
- Framework source: https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine
- CLI source and agent contract: https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli

Use public packages; applications must not import `github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/internal/...`. The CLI produces a project `spine.toml`, `go.mod`, root `main.go`, and composition under `internal/application`. The default `layered-v1` layout organizes code by role; `legacy` is available for existing feature-oriented projects.

## Install and create a project

```sh
go install github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-cli/cmd/spine@latest
spine version
spine new my-app --module example.com/my-app --channel main --no-interactive
cd my-app
spine doctor
spine contract check
spine verify
spine dev
```

`--channel main` chooses published stable dependency tags, `rc` selects a published RC or higher stable tag, and `preview` resolves the moving Preview branch. The interactive wizard defaults to Preview: select Main explicitly for a stable project. The selected value is stored as `dependency_channel` and reused by `spine update`. A new tool installation does not rewrite an existing app. When compatible stable platform tags are unavailable, use `--channel rc`; it may select a newer core RC. To reproduce core `v0.7.1` in a generated app, run `go get github.com/NARUBROWN/spine@v0.7.1` followed by `go mod tidy`, verify compatible platform versions, and retain the resolved files. `--skip-install` still resolves versions and metadata but skips installation and build verification.

`spine contract check` analyzes source without starting the application. `spine verify` also runs formatting, `go vet`, and tests; neither proves real HTTP, database, broker, or WebSocket behavior. After a `--skip-install` generation or dependency changes, run `go mod tidy` and `go mod download all` before the offline contract check. Test external dependencies separately.

For changes made by a generator, review the exact plan and apply the matching base hash:

```sh
spine g resource order --dry-run --json
spine g resource order --if-match <base_hash> --json
spine update --dry-run --json
spine update --if-match <base_hash> --json
```

Use the corresponding hash from each plan. A changed project or dependency resolution invalidates a reviewed plan. `spine update` changes the selected project dependencies, not the CLI executable, application source, or implementation selection. See `spine schema --json` and `spine capabilities --json` for the installed CLI's contract.

## Controllers and dependency injection

Use `api.Controller.RegisterRoutes(*api.Registry)` and register `constructor.Controller(&Controller{})` through `app.Constructor`. Constructor role markers include `Custom`, `Repository`, `Service`, `Controller`, and `Interceptor`; objects define `Constructor(dependencies...) *Self`. Function constructors remain supported and return exactly one value. Dependencies resolve by type. Existing `app.Route` and method expressions remain compatible but `app.Route` is deprecated. Duplicate method and path pairs are rejected during preparation.

This complete application is the tested introduction example. Install `github.com/NARUBROWN/spine@v0.7.1` and a compatible Echo platform in a Go module, save the code as `main.go`, run it, and request `/greeting`.

```go
package main

import (
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine"
	echoplatform "github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-echo-platform"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/api"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/boot"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/constructor"
	"github.com/NARUBROWN/spine/pkg/httpx"
	"log"
)

type Repository struct{}

func (*Repository) Constructor() *Repository { return &Repository{} }
func (*Repository) Greeting() string         { return "hello" }

type Service struct{ repository *Repository }

func (*Service) Constructor(repository *Repository) *Service { return &Service{repository: repository} }

type Controller struct{ service *Service }

func (*Controller) Constructor(service *Service) *Controller { return &Controller{service: service} }
func (c *Controller) RegisterRoutes(r *api.Registry) {
	r.GET("/greeting", func() httpx.Response[string] {
		return httpx.Response[string]{Body: c.service.repository.Greeting()}
	})
}
func main() {
	app := spine.New(echoplatform.Option())
	app.Constructor(
		constructor.Controller(&Controller{}),
		constructor.Service(&Service{}),
		constructor.Repository(&Repository{}),
	)
	if err := app.Run(boot.Options{Address: ":8080", HTTP: &boot.HTTPOptions{}}); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

Use `r.GET(path, handler, options...)` and the same order for group methods. Pass `api.Tags`, `api.Summary`, `api.Description`, and `api.Interceptors` after the handler. `api.Options` is not part of this release. Register a DI-managed interceptor's constructor and use a typed nil pointer in the route option when resolution from the container is required. See /en/learn/migration/preview-controller-routes and /en/learn/tutorial/4-interceptor.

## HTTP input, output, and errors

Use `input.Path[T]` for a struct or supported basic scalar, `input.Query[T]` and `input.Body[T]` for structs, and a separate struct pointer with `header` tags for headers. Struct path and query fields use their source tag or lowerCamel name. In v0.7.1, declare one scalar path input per route variable in route order; do not mix scalar inputs with a path DTO or legacy path wrappers. See /en/learn/tutorial/2-controller and /en/learn/core-concepts/query-values.

`query.Values`, `header.Values`, `query.Pagination`, and legacy `path.Int`, `path.String`, and `path.Boolean` are deprecated but remain compatible. Do not mix a deprecated input and a new Path, Query, or Header input in one handler. Body DTOs and contexts can accompany either. New typed inputs reject malformed numbers with HTTP 400. Use pointer fields to distinguish an absent query from zero; apply application defaults only when absent. Query slices support repeated keys, and comma-separated values when the HTTP platform exposes raw query. Register a validator explicitly for `validate` tags.

HTTP v3 uses core body parsing. It does not merge path or query into a body DTO or call Echo Binder and JSONSerializer extensions for Spine DTO input. The multipart memory threshold is not a total request-memory limit. Uploaded files are available through completion hooks and cleaned up afterwards; copy files needed later. Ordinary non-pointer JSON fields reject explicit null. Read /en/learn/migration/preview-features for content types, TLS, and request lifetime.

Return supported outputs such as `httpx.Response[T]`, `httpx.Redirect`, `httpx.Binary`, or an `error`. Use `httperr` for deliberate client errors; do not expose unexpected internal errors as client messages. Handler-selected status codes and handler-local defaults are not inferred by static OpenAPI.

## Interceptors and prepared applications

Global HTTP `PreHandle` executes before route selection and receives empty `HandlerMeta`; route interceptors run after routing and input binding. If authentication must precede body binding, use an HTTP-scoped global interceptor. `BeforeResponse` runs for interceptors whose `PreHandle` succeeded and may commit or roll back. `AfterCompletion` is for observation and cleanup, not changing an already transmitted response. A database commit, broker publication, and HTTP response are not one atomic operation.

`app.Prepare(ctx, options)` prepares without opening a listener, but may perform broker readiness checks or custom initialization. It returns `PreparedApplication`, whose `HTTPAdapter()` returns the prepared adapter and whose `Close(ctx)` releases resources. `spine.NetHTTPHandler(prepared)` returns `(http.Handler, error)` when supported. The caller shuts down its external server and closes the prepared result; do not start or stop the adapter twice. Prepared cleanup continues after a waiting context expires. See /en/reference/api/spine-app and /en/learn/migration/preview-features#prepared.

## OpenAPI, transports, and security

Runtime OpenAPI is disabled by default. Set `boot.HTTPOptions.OpenAPI.Enabled` and optionally register embedded Swagger UI and ReDoc via `UI`. Documentation paths are separate from `GlobalPrefix`; configure authentication in HTTP middleware or a proxy if needed. The CLI can also export a static document using `spine contract export --format openapi --output openapi.json`. Static analysis does not execute app initialization or infer dynamic code and all runtime validator constraints.

HTTP can use Echo or net/http. WebSocket needs an HTTP platform supporting upgrades and a separate Gorilla platform. Kafka, RabbitMQ, and NATS are independent event platforms. HTTP alone does not add WebSocket. The CLI supports `--platform nethttp`, `--websocket-platform gorilla`, repeated `--event-platform [name:]provider`, and `--validator playground`. Verify actual broker delivery and WebSocket exchanges; source inspection is not runtime evidence.

Use explicit origins, secure broker transports and environment-backed secrets. `cors.NewValidated` checks policy before accepting requests. Allowed preflight receives 204 and denied origin, method, or headers receive 403; ordinary CORS policy does not replace authentication. Kafka failed-offset handling can block a poison record; RabbitMQ requeue can repeat indefinitely. Use idempotent consumers and an outbox when database changes and event delivery require durable coordination. See /en/reference/security-configuration and /en/reference/examples/msa.

## External example details

### Bun ORM + Swagger: spine-user-demo

Reviewed snapshot: [`b07d2bb`](https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-user-demo/tree/b07d2bb35d6e0b499c6f6974e1d34f3a4fafffba), Go `1.25.5`, Spine `v0.5.1`.

Follow `HTTP -> controller -> service -> repository -> Bun -> MySQL`. Together, `main.go`, `routes/user_routes.go`, `interceptor/tx_interceptor.go`, `repository/user_repository.go`, and the transaction E2E show DI, `bun.IDB` reuse across `*bun.DB`/`bun.Tx`, response-aware rollback, error mapping, and Swaggo UI. Set `SPINE_DEMO_MYSQL_DSN`, run `go run . -migrate` before the first `go run .`, and open `/swagger/index.html`. Actual CRUD uses `/users?id=1`, not `/users/:id`, with no list endpoint; prefer code over mismatching README/generated fields.

### Kafka MSA: spine-simple-msa-demo

Reviewed snapshot: [`aa3f0fa`](https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-simple-msa-demo/tree/aa3f0fae8057ec0999fadaafc9295b7c7987afbb), Go `1.25.5`, Spine `v0.5.1`.

The repository name ends in `-demo`, but its `go.mod` module/import path is `github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-simple-msa`. Do not rewrite imports to add `-demo`.

The flow is `POST order -> order.created -> stock idempotency decision -> stock.reserved|stock.rejected -> order result consumer -> GET status`. Read both app `main.go` files, `shared/events`, and `scenarios/outbox`; run the stock worker then order HTTP service. Docker E2E uses Redpanda port `19092`, while manual defaults use Kafka `9092`. Topic prefix must include its separator and match both processes. JSON/in-memory stores are educational; production provisioning, keys, retention, schemas, retry topics, and DLQ remain application work.

### WebSocket chat: spine-simple-chat-demo

Reviewed snapshot: [`b1fe598`](https://github.com/NARUBROWN/spine-simple-chat-demo/tree/b1fe598329eb79828eb4c84903c7fa3847d35914), Go `1.25.5`, Spine `v0.5.1`.

This single-process in-memory server implements authenticated `join -> message -> leave`, one room per connection, room broadcast, typed errors, and runtime limit tests. Read its main, auth interceptor, controller, and E2E. Query `token` or exact `Authorization: Bearer ...` authenticates the handshake; the header wins, and blank config falls back to public `demo-token`, so production must override it and use `wss://`. There is no frontend, persistence, multi-instance state, or user/room authorization. Disconnect cleanup waits for a failed send; 1000-rune logical messages can exceed the 4096-byte frame limit; `leave` keeps the socket open. Build-tagged E2E requires a running server and `go test -tags=e2e -v ./e2e`.

## Agent implementation checklist

- Identify required transports, then read the closest example's actual `main.go`, handler, test, and `go.mod`.
- Define DTO/signature contracts, DI direction, idempotency key, transaction/outbox boundary, retry/DLQ policy, and shutdown behavior before wiring routes.
- Centralize assembly; use semantic inputs, supported outputs, narrow interceptor scopes, and environment-backed secrets.
- Check every registration/startup error; enable `HTTP` only where a listener is intended.
- Verify WebSocket origins/auth/capacity, secure broker transport, poison-message behavior, and durable consumer deduplication.
- Remember that `Validate` does not replace DI warm-up, route-ambiguity checks, or live consumer readiness in `Run`.

For Go changes, format the edited files, then run the CLI gates:

```sh
gofmt -w <changed-go-files>
spine contract check --json
spine verify --json
```

Run `go test -race ./...` separately when the change affects concurrency.

Run relevant broker/database/WebSocket E2E separately. For the historical external MSA demo only, run this PowerShell example from that demo repository root:

```powershell
$env:SPINE_DEMO_KAFKA_BROKER = "localhost:19092"
go run ./stock-app
```
